tagline: A shelf of pavement above the Hudson.
intro: From Cornwall-on-Hudson toward Highland Falls, Route 218 winds around Storm King Mountain as much as 420 feet above the Hudson. A rubblestone wall edges the river side, the grade never passes 7 percent, and no building of any kind stands along it.

Surveyors sometimes had to rappel down the cliffs to mark the line. A proposed tunnel gave way to an open road, which saved the cost of lighting it and kept the scenery in sight. Below ran the West Shore railroad, where dislodged boulders could block the tracks. When the road opened in 1922, it cut 22 miles off the drive from Newburgh to West Point.

moments.title: Camp Olmsted
moments.text: Since 1901 a Methodist mission from Manhattan's Five Points has kept a camp here for city children; the first campers came up the river on a Hudson River Day Liner.

moments.title: Storm King Highway pullouts
moments.text: Small pullouts along the mountainside road look across the Hudson toward Breakneck Ridge and Bull Hill.

moments.title: Highland Falls Village Hall
moments.text: A three-story brick building of about 1894 housed a bank for many years, became the village hall in 1967, and has gone without significant alteration since.

practical: Gates close the highway during heavy rain or snow because of rockfall, avalanche and falling-ice hazards.
